title: Office Partner says data held by an external service provider was accessed
date_note: Disclosed November 18; Office Partner says access began November 7.
summary: German office supplier Office Partner said unauthorised people accessed customer data stored at an external service provider from November 7. Names, addresses, phone numbers, invoices, account e-mail addresses and encrypted passwords were involved; payment data was not. It says it closed the gap, filed a criminal complaint and told the data protection authority.
plain: A German office supplier says hackers reached customer details, including encrypted passwords, through one of its service providers.
exec: Supplier-held customer data leaked; the number affected is not stated, but phishing against Office Partner customers (it says it has more than one million) becomes more convincing.
action: Office Partner customers: change your password here and anywhere you reused it, and be wary of unexpected messages.
impact: Customer contact data, invoices and encrypted passwords; company says it has more than one million customers.

validation.note: heise and ChannelPartner (citing the company's customer letter) report independently; both give 7 November as the start and exclude payment data.

review.note: Facts match heise; exec treated the company's own over-one-million customer base as the exposed population, reworded (affected count not stated)
